app.js.reason: Fail-closed candidate merge (answer/solution conflicts become sticky and block formal admission) plus teacher-facing reliability fixes: the remembered view is restored before the first await, and a failed card edit is reported and rolled back to the stored truth. Then the deterministic MathType/MTEF restoration: the app's existing DOCX extraction path resolves each MathType OLE object through Qisi.DocxPipeline, keeps the formula evidence per file, and never reads the OLE control text. 2026-09-16: the DOCX SILENT WRONG CONTENT fix - the paragraph reader only reads real text elements (no structural element can become text), the flat question splitter moved to qisi-utils with the mark-sheet and image-token marker rules, and option evidence is only accepted from text that belongs to the question being filled. Then the support-file active anchor and the missing explicit answer rule: an answer/solution marker may sit behind an inline image token, and a 详解 conclusion such as 故选C is reported to the teacher but never written into the answer field. Then the withheld question rule: a question that still carries an unresolved MathType formula keeps the token visible, is marked withheld with rejected provenance for the affected field, and cannot be admitted until a teacher fills it in, while the option-label normalizer no longer rewrites the token's own tail. Then the section-header and answer-value rules found while verifying the remaining real groups: a section header without a colon types its questions, and an answer written without a label keeps its own value instead of being dropped. Then the answer-key stream rule: a key is located by its heading and read as one sequence of number/value entries, so several answers per line and wrapped lines no longer lose the key, while a value that crosses a line break is dropped rather than swallowing an orphan fragment. Continuous ingestion audit: deterministic DOCX orchestration replaces conversion/vision-first; shared extraction, automatic numbering, image gaps and no order-based support writes.
